Definition: to cover (specifically with bitumen); figuratively, to expiate or condone, to placate or cancel
BiblicalUsage: Kaphar is to cover — with pitch, with a gift, with blood — and so to expiate, to make atonement. Jacob says, I will appease Esau with the present that goeth before me; the priest lays his hand on the burnt offering and it is accepted to make atonement; the coal touches Isaiah's lips and his sin is purged; and Daniel hears that seventy weeks are determined to make reconciliation for iniquity.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this is the heart of the whole Bible: sin is covered, not by pretending it is not there, but by a gift, a sacrifice, and a Saviour — and the covering God provides is the one that stands. The blood covers what the gift and the sacrifice point to, and the Saviour finishes it.
